With positive power ($P = 36\text{ kW}$), the driving force $D = \frac{P}{v} > 0$ always exceeds resistance balance, meaning the car continues to accelerate without reaching a finite steady speed under constant non-zero resistance.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Downhill driving force at $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is $900\text{ N}$. Downhill gravity ($600\text{ N}$) cancels resistance ($600\text{ N}$):
$$a = \frac{900 + 600 - 600}{1200} = \frac{900}{1200} = 0.75\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

For steady speed down the hill, forces must balance:
$$D = R - mg\sin\alpha = 600 - 600 = 0\text{ N}$$
Hence no finite steady speed exists under constant $P = 36\text{ kW}$ unless resistance increases with speed.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the weight component down the slope:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = 16000(10)(0.02) = 3200\text{ N}$$
At steady maximum speed $V$:
$$D = R + W_{\parallel} \implies \frac{120000}{V} = (800 + 20V) + 3200$$
$$\frac{120000}{V} = 20V + 4000$$

Multiply throughout by $V$:
$$120000 = 20V^2 + 4000V \implies 20V^2 + 4000V - 120000 = 0$$
Divide through by 20:
$$V^2 + 200V - 6000 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:
$$V = \frac{-200 \pm \sqrt{200^2 - 4(1)(-6000)}}{2} = \frac{-200 \pm \sqrt{40000 + 24000}}{2} = \frac{-200 \pm \sqrt{64000}}{2}$$
Since $V > 0$:
$$V = \frac{-200 + 252.98}{2} = \frac{52.98}{2} \approx 26.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Form monic quadratic:
$$20V^2 + 4000V - 120000 = 0 \implies V^2 + 200V - 6000 = 0$$
